symbols.name: LOGIN_WINDOW
doc: I COUNT WRONG PASSWORDS, and a key with too many in 15 minutes is refused without even checking the password (so guessing cannot go on, and a refused try costs no bcrypt work). I use three keys: one ticket from one address (the person typing his own password wrongly: 6), one address (a script trying many tickets: 30), one ticket from anywhere (many addresses at one account: 40). A correct password clears the first. The tables live in one server copy (see src/lib/security/rateLimit.ts for what that can and cannot do).

symbols.name: failsPair
symbols.sig: const failsPair = createFailureLock({ max: 6, windowMs: LOGIN_WINDOW })

symbols.name: failsTicket
symbols.sig: const failsTicket = createFailureLock({ max: 40, windowMs: LOGIN_WINDOW })

symbols.name: DUMMY_HASH
doc: A real bcrypt hash of a password nobody has. I check an unknown ticket against it so that "no such ticket" and "wrong password" take the same time (no way to find which tickets exist by timing).
